summary: Jean Dantinne was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Filliozat (1906–1982) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1928–1934), held a chair at the Collège de France (1951–1978), and directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1956–1977).

Jean Philippe Vogel (1871–1958) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. After studying at the University of Amsterdam (~1890–1897), he worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1910–1911) and served as director at Leiden University (attested 1910; 1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski (1885–1944) studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1912–1920), later serving there as directeur d'études (~1926–1930). Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, he also taught at INALCO (1923) and the Collège de France (~1930–1944).

Jean-Baptiste Biot (1774–1862) studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand, École polytechnique, and École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées. Working in sinology and history/archaeology, he held posts at the French Revolutionary Army, Bureau des Longitudes, Collège de France (1800–1862), and Science Faculty of Paris (1809–1862).
Jean-François Jarrige (1940–2014) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Lycée Claude Fauriel and École du Louvre (~1961–1964), later heading the Musée Guimet (~1986–2008).

Jean-Louis Burnouf (1775–1844) studied at Collège d'Harcourt and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. A linguist, he held posts at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1826), University of Paris (~1817–1826), École Normale Supérieure (~1826–1838), and Collège de France (1817–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Jean-Luc Chevillard (born 1956) works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1975 and served as a researcher at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1991–2021).

Jean-Noël Robert (born 1949) studied at INALCO and under Bernard Frank. A specialist in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology, he held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–2011) and the Collège de France (2011–2022).
Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (1788–1832) was a sinologist and linguist who studied at INALCO. He served as Professor of Chinese at the Collège de France from 1815 until 1832.

Jeannine Auboyer (1912–1990) specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at École du Louvre, Académie Julian, and EPHE, later working at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1942–1965) and the Musée Guimet (1965–1980).
Jeff Dolven studied at Yale University (~1984–1988) and Worcester College (~1989–1991). He held a post at Princeton University around 1998.
Jeff Malpas (born 1958) is a philosopher who served as a professor at the University of Tasmania (~1999) and held a post at La Trobe University in 2019.
Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and was mentored by Taitetsu Unno and Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long (born 1969) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1993–2000) and became Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College (~2000).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff studied at Missouri State University and UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White, Barbara A. Holdrege, and William F. Powell. In religious studies and Indology, he held posts at UCSB, UC, and Marshall University (2002).
Jeffrey Davis Schoening specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. in 1991 at the University of Washington, where he studied under advisors Sanghasen Singh and Collett Cox.

Jeffrey Hopkins (1940–2024) studied under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Gelden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. ~1968–1972). In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he was a professor and center director at the University of Virginia (1973–2024).

Jeffrey J. Kripal (born 1962) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College (~1981–1985) and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1987–1993), later holding an associate professorship at Rice University (~2002).
